newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bank loans option in Fina deal - PetroFina.
newsitem.headline: Bank loans option in Fina deal - PetroFina.

text.p: Belgian oil and energy group PetroFina said in Tuesday its $60 a share bid for stock in its U.S. unit Fina Inc which it does not already own could be financed through bank loans.
PetroFina spokeswoman Catherine Ferrant told Reuters, "(The financing) could be through bank lending if necessary...we have a good rating...our debt is seen positively in the financial markets."
The exact way in which the $266 million bid will be funded will be the subject of negotiations with Fina's independent directors, who are also included among Fina's shareholders.
Ferrant said PetroFina would seek to buy back any PetroFina shares issued as a result of the proposed takeover to avoid increasing the total number of shares outstanding.
The bid is for 14.6 percent of Fina's capital now held by Fina employees, Fina officers and directors, holders of depository receipts listed in Brussels and U.S. institutional investors.

A planned listing of PetroFina shares on the New York Stock Exchange or the expiry of a warrant issue in three months' time would not be used to raise money for the transaction. "There is no link," Ferrant said.

Between May 20 and June 3, 1,162,611 warrants can be exercised at a ratio of one share for one warrant with the price for the share set at 12,500 Belgian francs. That compares with Tuesday's closing price of 12,300, up 0.2 percent on the day.
The warrant closed at 482 francs, up 38 francs. The paper has risen sharply since January 22 when it closed at 202 francs, breaking above its May 1996 high of 378.

Asked about the reason behind the takeover of Fina, Ferrant said, "It is logical in the context of the evolution of the company. We have been looking at this for a long time. Independent (Fina) shareholders had been asking for it."
"We have the possibility to do so in view of our growth and our growth perspective."

Trade in Fina shares on the OTC market in New York was halted at 0947 EST (0447 GMT) with the last trade at $50, down 1/8 of a dollar. In Brussels Fina trade was halted at 1542 local at a price of 1,700 francs, down 5 francs.
PetroFina, which employs 14,000 people in 50 countries, had estimated 1996 turnover of about $470 million, an increase of 36 percent from 1995.
Major refineries and petrochemical plants are in Belgium, England and Italy.
Under the Fina brandname a service station network includes 4,000 outlets in Europe.
Chemical sales focus on high-density polyethylene, polypropylene and polystyrene.
